s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of systemic and neurological symptoms with fever, encephalopathy, and multi-organ involvement
salient_findings: Generalized weakness, weight loss, and altered mental status
Worsening encephalopathy and inability to tolerate oral intake
Chorea involving left upper and lower extremities
Painful vesicular oral and genital lesions
Severe odynophagia and hypersalivation
key_facts: Several months history of headaches, fevers, nausea, and malaise
Temperature 38.1°C at initial presentation
Leukocytosis (21 × 10³/μL) with elevated C-reactive protein and sedimentation rate
Mild iron deficiency anemia
Normal blood cultures, urinalysis, lactic acid, and immunologic panel
Lymphocytic pleocytosis with mixed inflammatory cells in cerebrospinal fluid
Glucose: 43 mg/dL, Protein: 80 mg/dL, RBC: 3 cells/μL in cerebrospinal fluid
Positive West Nile virus IgG, negative IgM
Negative autoimmune encephalitis panel
Hyperintensities in thalami, midbrain, and pons on T2 FLAIR MRI
Lesions isolated to lips and buccal mucosa, and scrotum and penile shaft

shortlist.label: West Nile Virus Encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive West Nile virus IgG and clinical presentation of encephalopathy and fever

shortlist.label: Herpes Simplex Encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presentation of encephalopathy, fever, and lesions, which are common in herpes simplex encephalitis

shortlist.label: Varicella-Zoster Virus Encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of encephalopathy, fever, and painful vesicular oral and genital lesions

shortlist.label: Behcet Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Multi-organ involvement, including oral and genital lesions, and neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of encephalopathy, fever, and potential for multi-organ involvement

raw.rationale: The presence of painful vesicular oral and genital lesions, altered mental status, and hyperintensities in the thalami, midbrain, and pons on T2 FLAIR MRI are more consistent with Herpes Simplex Encephalitis, despite the positive West Nile virus IgG. The clinical presentation and imaging findings are more typical of Herpes Simplex Encephalitis.

rejected.label: West Nile Virus Encephalitis
rejected.why: The presence of painful vesicular oral and genital lesions and the specific MRI findings are not typical of West Nile Virus Encephalitis, and the positive IgG without IgM suggests past infection rather than acute disease.

rejected.label: Varicella-Zoster Virus Encephalitis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings do not specifically suggest Varicella-Zoster Virus Encephalitis, and there is no mention of a rash or dermatomal distribution of lesions.

rejected.label: Behcet Disease
rejected.why: While Behcet Disease can cause oral and genital lesions, the combination of encephalopathy, hyperintensities on MRI, and cerebrospinal fluid findings are not typical of Behcet Disease.

rejected.label: Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: Toxoplasmosis typically presents with focal neurologic deficits and mass lesions on imaging, which are not present in this case.
